feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible: point/column-scale water-balance partitioning (P into ET, surface runoff, and deep drainage/recharge) is fully answerable with single-column ELM run over representative elevation/land-cover bands; basin-integrated streamflow validation at a gauge is only approximate because single-column ELM performs no lateral routing.
answerable: Long-term and seasonal partitioning of precipitation into evapotranspiration (EFLX_LH_TOT/QFLX_EVAP_TOT), surface runoff (QOVER), and deep drainage/recharge (QDRAI) at each representative column.
Elevation-gradient controls on snow accumulation/melt (H2OSNO, QSNOMELT) and its influence on runoff timing.
Vegetation vs. soil evaporation vs. transpiration breakdown of ET (QVEGE, QVEGT, QSOIL).
Column-level closure of the water balance (P = ET + total runoff + dS) and recharge fraction of precipitation.
Point validation of ET against nearby flux-tower / MODIS ET and SWE against SNOTEL where co-located.
not_answerable: Basin-outlet discharge hydrograph and its timing/magnitude (requires a routing model, e.g., MOSART, coupled to gridded ELM).
Spatially explicit, area-weighted HUC8 water budget without an off-line areal weighting/aggregation step across many more grid cells.
Lateral groundwater flow, baseflow separation, and stream-aquifer exchange (needs PFLOTRAN-coupled subsurface or a groundwater model).
Direct comparison to USGS gauge 12494000 (Naches near mouth) streamflow as a validation of 'runoff' from a single column.

parsed.n_justification: The Naches (HUC8 17030002) spans a strong west-to-east climatic and ecological gradient from the wet, snow-dominated Cascade crest (~1800 m, coniferous forest) down to semi-arid shrub-steppe near the valley outlet (~500 m). Five columns capture the dominant hydrologic response units (high alpine/subalpine, upper montane forest, mid-elevation mixed forest, lower forest/foothill, and valley shrub-steppe) that control the snow/rain split, ET demand, and recharge, which is the minimum needed to represent the partitioning gradient while keeping the campaign tractable.
requires_capabilities: Single-column (single-point) ELM configuration (I-compset, e.g., I1850/I20TR-style datm forcing) with site-specific surface dataset generation per column.
Atmospheric forcing (GSWP3 or CLMNCEP/CRUNCEP) available and downscaled/bias-corrected to the column elevations; elevation-lapse correction recommended.
Spin-up capability (accelerated + final CN/BGC spin-up) prior to the 1980-2014 transient run to equilibrate soil moisture and water table.
Post-processing to compute per-column water-balance closure and recharge fraction; optional areal weighting to approximate HUC8-integrated fluxes.
Observational datasets for validation: USGS streamflow (gauge 12494000), SNOTEL SWE stations within the basin, MODIS/AmeriFlux ET, and USGS/soil-water-balance recharge estimates.
assumptions: Deep drainage flux (QDRAI, with QCHARGE to the aquifer) is used as the proxy for groundwater recharge at each column.
Total runoff is QRUNOFF (QOVER surface + QDRAI subsurface); no lateral routing is applied, so column runoff is a vertical-flux estimate, not gauge discharge.
Columns are treated as independent 1-D profiles; HUC8 aggregation is done offline via area weighting of the five HRU-representative columns, not via lateral connectivity.
GSWP3-class forcing at ~0.5 deg is downscaled to each column's elevation; snow/rain partitioning sensitivity to forcing temperature is acknowledged as a key uncertainty.
Soil textures assigned per column are representative estimates (SSURGO/STATSGO-informed) and used to set hydraulic properties in the surface dataset.
35-year transient window (1980-2014) provides robust long-term means and interannual variability for partitioning; a multi-decade spin-up precedes it.
Water-year (Oct-Sep) accounting is used for seasonal partitioning to align with snow-dominated hydrology.
